name: interlace-base
title: Interlace Base
description: @interlace/ui — the additive CSS baseline every component needs: motion tokens, type scale, container widths, the xs breakpoint, radius derived from --radius, layered brand + semantic colour tokens in OKLCH, and a color-scheme that follows the dark class so native controls match. Changes nothing the host app already styles.
author: ofri-peretz <https://github.com/ofri-peretz>

files.content:
/*
 * @interlace/ui — BRAND: the Interlace palette, light + dark.
 *
 * Layer 1 of 4 (brand → semantics → structure → page). This file holds raw
 * values and nothing else: every declaration is an `--interlace-*` literal
 * inside `@layer interlace.brand`. It never names a shadcn token and nothing
 * outside `semantics.css` reads it. `__tests__/css-layer-lock.test.ts`
 * holds both rules.
 *
 * A theme is a sibling of this file (brand/harbor.css) that overrides the
 * same `--interlace-*` keys under `[data-theme='<name>']`. Forking the brand
 * means writing one more of these, not touching the alias graph.
 *
 * ─── Two orthogonal axes: scheme × theme ──────────────────────────
 *
 * A colour SCHEME and a THEME are different questions and must not share a
 * selector. Until Phase 8 they did: the dark block was keyed on
 * `.dark, [data-theme='dark']`, which spends the `data-theme` attribute —
 * the only obvious place to put "which brand" — on "which scheme".
 *
 *   scheme  →  light | dark              (`.dark` / `[data-scheme='dark']`)
 *   theme   →  interlace | harbor | …    (`[data-theme='<name>']`)
 *
 * | Selector                        | Means                                |
 * |---------------------------------|--------------------------------------|
 * | `:root`                         | interlace · light  (the default)     |
 * | `.dark`, `[data-scheme='dark']` | interlace · dark                     |
 * | `[data-theme='X']`              | theme X · light   (brand/X.css)      |
 * | `[data-theme='X'].dark`         | theme X · dark    (brand/X.css)      |
 *
 * `.dark` stays load-bearing on purpose: it is the shadcn / next-themes
 * convention, every consumer and the Storybook `withThemeByClassName`
 * decorator write it, and breaking it to gain a cleaner name would be
 * vanity. The new axis is purely ADDITIVE — nothing that worked before
 * stopped working, with one deliberate exception: `[data-theme='dark']` no
 * longer means "dark scheme". It now reads as "the theme named dark", which
 * is not a registered theme, so it resolves to interlace · light. Consumers
 * on that spelling move to `[data-scheme='dark']` (or `.dark`).
 *
 * Every theme file declares into `@layer interlace.brand` and overrides ONLY
 * `--interlace-*` colour values. semantics.css and its `@theme inline`
 * block never change — that is the whole point of the
 * cascade, and it is why a theme is a data file rather than a pile of CSS.
 * `THEME_TOKENS` (src/lib/theme-tokens.ts) enumerates every token a theme
 * must define, and `__tests__/theme-contract-lock.test.ts` fails on a theme
 * that omits one — because a missing token does not throw, it silently
 * inherits the PREVIOUS theme's value and ships a two-brand page nobody
 * notices.
 *
 * Contrast contract (WCAG 2.2 AA):
 *   - Body text on background: ≥ 4.5:1 (target: 7:1 AAA where possible)
 *   - Large text + UI controls on adjacent surface: ≥ 3:1
 *   - Focus ring on adjacent colors: ≥ 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.13)
 *   - Verified at https://webaim.org/resources/contrastchecker/ — every
 *     primary/foreground pair below clears the floor for its mode.
 *
 * Source palette: the Interlace mark — burnt orange (see render-cover.sh).
 *   Light primary: #7d350c → 8.80:1 on white (AAA)
 *   Dark primary:  #fbb99a → 11.63:1 on the dark page #0e0c0a (AAA)
 *
 * Replaced the Tailwind-violet palette this system shipped with. Every pair
 * below was re-measured after the swap; none regressed.
 *
 * Written in OKLCH. Lightness, chroma and hue are separate numbers, so a
 * hover step is "a little darker" in one place and a new theme can keep the
 * hue and move only the lightness. Each value was chosen to paint exactly
 * the sRGB pixel the hex it replaced painted (checked in Chromium), so every
 * ratio quoted in these comments, and every one the contrast locks measure,
 * is unchanged. The hex quoted beside a value in prose is that pixel.
 * apps/registry/public/tokens/interlace.tokens.json carries the same palette
 * in the Design Tokens (DTCG) format for design tools; it is generated from
 * this file.
 */


@layer interlace.brand {
  /* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *  LIGHT — default
   * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  :root,
  [data-scheme='light'] {
    /* Brand
     *
     * Burnt orange, from the mark. #7d350c measures 8.80:1 on white, 8.12:1
     * on `--accent` (#fef4ed), and 7.46:1 on its OWN 10% tint — that last one
     * is the binding constraint. `bg-primary/10` + `text-primary` is a stock
     * shadcn badge pattern, and it composites to #f3ebe7 on white; a lighter
     * orange (#8a3a10) landed at 6.63:1 there and axe failed the enhanced
     * check. This value tracks violet-800's old profile (8.98 / 7.56) so the
     * AAA floor holds on every catalogue surface AND on brand-tinted ones. */
    --interlace-primary: oklch(0.422 0.1117 45.2);            /* 8.80:1 on white (AAA) */
    --interlace-primary-hover: oklch(0.375 0.1011 44);      /* 10.63:1 on white */
    --interlace-primary-active: oklch(0.305 0.0758 44.7);     /* 13.76:1 on white */
    --interlace-primary-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);
    --interlace-primary-subtle: oklch(0.973 0.0143 57.6);     /* warm tint for backgrounds */
    --interlace-primary-subtle-foreground: oklch(0.305 0.0758 44.7);  /* 12.70:1 on subtle (AAA) */

    /* Surface
     *
     * The page is warm paper (#fdfbf8), not screen white, and cards and
     * popovers stay white so they lift off it the way a sheet lifts off a
     * desk. The tone is as warm as it can go while primary holds 8.5:1 on
     * it (8.52:1) and 7.23:1 on its own 10% tint over it, so the binding
     * constraint above still clears AAA on the page as well as on a card.
     * Foreground 19.02:1, muted-foreground 9.11:1, `--input` 3.50:1. */
    --interlace-background: oklch(0.989 0.0045 78);
    --interlace-foreground: oklch(0.151 0.0055 67.8);         /* near-black, slight warm tint */
    --interlace-card: oklch(1 0 0);
    --interlace-card-foreground: oklch(0.151 0.0055 67.8);
    --interlace-popover: oklch(1 0 0);
    --interlace-popover-foreground: oklch(0.151 0.0055 67.8);
    --interlace-muted: oklch(0.978 0.0051 67.8);              /* warm-tinted neutral */
    --interlace-muted-foreground: oklch(0.396 0.0183 70.5);   /* 8.06:1 on white (AAA body); darkened from #6b6580 to clear AA even under axe sub-pixel rounding on hairline text */
    --interlace-border: oklch(0.929 0.0075 80.7);    /* 1.23:1 on white — decorative separators only, exempt from 1.4.11 */
    /* `--input` is the BOUNDARY of a form control (input / textarea / select
     * trigger / checkbox / radio / switch track), so WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11
     * (Non-text Contrast, AA) demands ≥3:1 against the adjacent surface —
     * the border is the only thing identifying the control.
     *
     * It used to alias `--border` (#eae7e2 → 1.23:1 on white): every
     * unfocused field in the DS was effectively invisible to a low-vision
     * user. Forked to a warm mid-grey that clears the floor while keeping
     * the brand's warm cast. Decorative `--border` deliberately stays soft. */
    --interlace-input: oklch(0.622 0.0202 70.1);              /* 3.62:1 on a white card, 3.50:1 on the #fdfbf8 page (SC 1.4.11 AA) */
    --interlace-ring: var(--interlace-primary);

    /* Accent */
    --interlace-accent: oklch(0.973 0.0143 57.6);             /* warm tint */
    --interlace-accent-foreground: oklch(0.397 0.1047 44.2);  /* 8.98:1 on accent (AAA) */

    /* Secondary */
    --interlace-secondary: oklch(0.965 0.0045 78.3);
    --interlace-secondary-foreground: oklch(0.222 0.0123 67.1);

    /* Destructive (Tailwind red-800 — bumped from red-700 #b91c1c (6.4:1) so
     * text-destructive on white clears WCAG 2.2 AAA (≥7:1) for normal body
     * text. red-800 #991b1b ≈ 8.0:1. */
    --interlace-destructive: oklch(0.444 0.1613 26.9);
    --interlace-destructive-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Success (Tailwind emerald-800 — bumped from emerald-600 #059669 (3.7:1).
     * text-success on white now ≈ 7.3:1, clearing AAA. The original brand
     * green stays available for bg-success surfaces (paired with white
     * foreground) where the contrast is between surface and foreground, not
     * surface and parent. */
    --interlace-success: oklch(0.432 0.0865 166.9);
    --interlace-success-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Warning (Tailwind amber-900 — bumped from amber-600 #d97706 (3.5:1).
     * Yellow on white can't physically clear 7:1 at its brand-bright value,
     * so the text token drops to amber-900 #78350f ≈ 8.5:1. For "yellow
     * background" treatments, pair `bg-amber-500` (decorative bg) with
     * `text-warning` (this token) — contrast is then warning on amber, not
     * warning on white. */
    --interlace-warning: oklch(0.414 0.1054 45.9);
    --interlace-warning-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Info (Tailwind blue-800 — new semantic token. text-info on white ≈
     * 8.5:1, AAA. Pair with bg-info-foreground for filled surfaces. */
    --interlace-info: oklch(0.424 0.1809 265.6);
    --interlace-info-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Caution — the rung BETWEEN warning and destructive. Scorecard ladders
     * need five distinguishable tones (excellent / good / fair / poor /
     * fail); without this token `poor` had no home and GradeBadge reached
     * outside the palette for a raw `bg-orange-900`. Tailwind orange-900
     * #7c2d12 ≈ 9.0:1 on white and stays hue-distinct from `--warning`
     * (amber-900 #78350f) at a glance while sharing the warm family. */
    --interlace-caution: oklch(0.408 0.1165 38.2);
    --interlace-caution-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Highlight — a warm call-to-action surface that is NOT the brand
     * primary: the "read this one" chip, the featured card, the second
     * button on a hero. A highlighter-pen amber (amber-300) so it stays
     * separable from the burnt-orange primary and the orange-900 caution
     * rung. Text sits dark on it: #1c1917 on #fcd34d ≈ 12.1:1 (AAA). */
    --interlace-highlight: oklch(0.879 0.1534 91.6);
    --interlace-highlight-foreground: oklch(0.216 0.0061 56);

    /* Scrim — the dark wash laid over an arbitrary image so text on top
     * stays legible (featured article covers, media overlays). Like the
     * hero surface these do NOT invert: the scrim's whole job is to be
     * darker than whatever photo sits under it, in either colour scheme.
     * Always used with a Tailwind alpha modifier (`bg-scrim/70`) — the
     * solid values are the ramp's endpoints, not what ships on screen.
     * #ffffff on #000000/70 over a mid-tone cover measures ≥ 7:1. */
    --interlace-scrim: oklch(0 0 0);
    --interlace-scrim-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    /* Cosmic hero effects — the three colours the starfield preset paints
     * onto <canvas> / SVG gradients (shooting-star head, its trail, meteor
     * streak). They live in the brand layer because the hero is the most
     * brand-visible surface we ship, and because canvas ignores the
     * cascade: HeroCosmic resolves these at runtime rather than letting a
     * vendored default paint the pre-brand violet palette (R19).
     *
     * The hero always renders on a deep near-black gradient in BOTH modes
     * (it is its own surface, not a themed one), so these do not invert. */
    --interlace-hero-star: oklch(0.839 0.0877 46.2);   /* brand orange tint — star head */
    --interlace-hero-trail: oklch(0.589 0.13186 159.35);  /* brand green — trail gradient */
    --interlace-hero-meteor: oklch(0.904 0.0515 48.8); /* palest orange — meteor streak */

    /* Cosmic hero surface. The hero is its OWN surface, not a themed one:
     * a starfield only reads as a starfield on near-black, so these do not
     * invert with the colour scheme. That is exactly why they need their
     * own tokens — reaching for `--background` / `--foreground` here would
     * paint black text on a black hero in light mode (the bug this pair
     * replaces). #f0ede9 on #0d0b09 measures 16.4:1 (AAA). */
    --interlace-hero-surface: oklch(0.151 0.0055 67.8);      /* gradient midpoint */
    --interlace-hero-surface-deep: oklch(0 0 0); /* gradient floor */
    --interlace-hero-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);   /* 16.4:1 on the surface (AAA) */

    /* Window controls — the three macOS traffic-light dots used by the
     * CodeWindow chrome. Purely decorative (the dot row is `aria-hidden`),
     * but they live here so a consumer forking the brand can restyle the
     * chrome without patching component source. Values are the macOS
     * system colours the affordance is quoting. */
    --interlace-window-control-close: oklch(0.694 0.1964 26.4);
    --interlace-window-control-minimize: oklch(0.835 0.1612 80.9);
    --interlace-window-control-zoom: oklch(0.728 0.2173 144.7);

    /* Chart palette — five distinct hues for series colors, brand-owned
     * so consumers can fork via `@layer interlace.brand`. Values match the
     * existing oklch ladder in theme.css (≥4.5:1 on bg-card light); the
     * promotion here makes the chart series an explicit brand surface
     * with `@layer interlace.brand` override semantics like every other
     * brand-coupled token. */
    /* Strands — the woven brand gesture (BRAND_PHILOSOPHY.md).
     *
     * strand-a is the mark's burnt orange (hue 41, same profile as
     * chart-1). strand-b is its temperature complement, a cool steel
     * blue (hue 230) — NOT chart-2's emerald (hue 162), which is the
     * success status hue; status colors are never decorative. The pair
     * is the only palette permitted in woven gestures (InterlaceWeave,
     * HeroStrand, TimelineMap marks + link threads), and woven gestures
     * are the only place strand-b may appear. Strokes: ≥3:1 both modes. */
    --interlace-strand-a: oklch(0.55 0.16 41);
    --interlace-strand-b: oklch(0.55 0.12 230);

    --interlace-chart-1: oklch(0.55 0.16 41);   /* brand orange */
    --interlace-chart-2: oklch(0.55 0.14 162);  /* brand green */
    --interlace-chart-3: oklch(0.55 0.18 264);  /* blue */
    --interlace-chart-4: oklch(0.55 0.14 90);   /* olive */
    --interlace-chart-5: oklch(0.55 0.13 200);  /* cyan */

    /* Visualisation chrome — the parts of a chart that are NOT the series.
     *
     * `--chart-N` answers "which line is which". These answer "what is the
     * line drawn on": gridlines, axis, graph edges. Three colour values; every
     * other `--viz-*` token in the semantics layer is a var() alias of an
     * already-AA-verified token, so a brand fork has three numbers to pick,
     * not fifteen. Warm-neutral to sit with the brand, not the cool greys.
     *
     * Contrast, measured against `--interlace-card` #ffffff (charts sit on
     * cards; on the #fdfbf8 page every ratio below falls by about 3%, and the
     * axis still clears 3:1):
     *   grid  #e0dad2 → 1.39:1  DECORATIVE. Gridlines must never be the sole
     *                           carrier of a value — that is what the axis
     *                           labels and the sr-only table are for. Kept
     *                           deliberately below 3:1 so a dense grid does
     *                           not fight the series it exists to support.
     *   axis  #8d857a → 3.64:1  Clears WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 (3:1, non-text UI
     *                           boundary). The axis IS structural — it is what
     *                           tells you where zero is.
     *   edge  #e0dad2 → 1.39:1  Ambient graph texture, same weight as grid.
     *                           An edge that MEANS something (selected, on the
     *                           highlighted path) switches to `--viz-edge-active`
     *                           (= `--primary`). Same split as the slider rail
     *                           vs knob: the low-contrast element is
     *                           supplementary, the high-contrast one carries
     *                           the success criterion. */
    --interlace-viz-grid: oklch(0.891 0.0127 75.4);
    --interlace-viz-axis: oklch(0.62 0.0189 76);
    --interlace-viz-edge: oklch(0.891 0.0127 75.4);

    /* Radius base — every rounded-* step derives from it (see
     * structure/type.css): sm 8px, md 10px, lg 12px, xl 16px at 0.75rem. */
    --interlace-radius: 0.75rem;

    /* Brand mark — bar fills for the two-bar Interlace mark (nav lockups;
     * see packages/ui/src/patterns/brand-logo.tsx). Decorative fills, not
     * text, so they track the favicon pair rather than the AAA text ramp.
     * Values match the eslint.interlace.tools nav mark. */
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-o: oklch(0.527 0.136 45.9);
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-g: oklch(0.468 0.101 160.9);
  }

  /* ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
   *  INTERLACE · DARK — the scheme axis.
   *
   *  `.dark` is the shadcn / next-themes class every consumer already
   *  writes; `[data-scheme='dark']` is the attribute spelling for hosts
   *  that would rather not touch className. They are the SAME axis, and
   *  neither of them says anything about which brand is active — that is
   *  `[data-theme]`, handled in styles/themes/*.css.
   * ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
  .dark,
  [data-scheme='dark'] {
    /* Brand — inverted weight: a light tint of the same burnt orange, so
     * both directions clear AAA. text-primary on the dark page is 11.63:1,
     * and bg-primary with text-primary-foreground (#0a0a0a) is 11.79:1.
     * The cover orange #f4794a is only 7.24:1 here, too dark to carry the
     * bidirectional pair, hence the lighter tint. */
    --interlace-primary: oklch(0.839 0.0877 46.2);            /* 11.63:1 on dark bg #0e0c0a (AAA) */
    --interlace-primary-hover: oklch(0.874 0.0674 47.5);      /* 13.31:1 */
    --interlace-primary-active: oklch(0.904 0.0515 48.8);     /* 14.68:1 */
    --interlace-primary-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0); /* near-black — 11.79:1 on primary */
    --interlace-primary-subtle: oklch(0.265 0.0617 45.7);     /* tinted background */
    --interlace-primary-subtle-foreground: oklch(0.904 0.0515 48.8);  /* 11.54:1 on subtle (AAA) */

    /* Surface */
    --interlace-background: oklch(0.155 0.0045 60);           /* warm near-black #0e0c0a, the paper's night side; primary 11.63:1, muted-foreground 11.16:1 */
    --interlace-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);
    --interlace-card: oklch(0.194 0.0063 56);
    --interlace-card-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);
    --interlace-popover: oklch(0.194 0.0063 56);
    --interlace-popover-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);
    --interlace-muted: oklch(0.194 0.0063 56);
    --interlace-muted-foreground: oklch(0.82 0.0129 75.3);   /* 11.16:1 on #0e0c0a (AAA); brightened from #a09cb3 (4.94:1) to clear AA even when stories render against `bg-fd-card/50` tinted surfaces */
    --interlace-border: oklch(0.247 0.0149 76.2);    /* 1.22:1 on near-black — decorative separators only */
    /* Dark counterpart of the SC 1.4.11 fork above. #252019 measured
     * 1.22:1 on `--background` — same invisible-control failure as light. */
    --interlace-input: oklch(0.504 0.0173 70.7);              /* 3.31:1 on #0e0c0a (SC 1.4.11 AA) */
    --interlace-ring: var(--interlace-primary);

    /* Accent */
    --interlace-accent: oklch(0.265 0.0617 45.7);             /* deep warm tint */
    --interlace-accent-foreground: oklch(0.874 0.0674 47.5);  /* 10.46:1 on accent (AAA) */

    /* Secondary */
    --interlace-secondary: oklch(0.229 0.0112 73.4);
    --interlace-secondary-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);

    /* Destructive (red-300 — bumped from red-500 #ef4444 (~5.2:1) so
     * text-destructive on near-black clears AAA. red-300 #fca5a5 ≈ 9:1. */
    --interlace-destructive: oklch(0.808 0.1035 19.6);
    --interlace-destructive-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);

    /* Success (emerald-400 — bumped from emerald-500 #10b981 (~6.3:1) for
     * AAA on dark. emerald-400 #34d399 ≈ 8.5:1. */
    --interlace-success: oklch(0.773 0.1535 163.2);
    --interlace-success-foreground: oklch(0.266 0.0628 152.9);

    /* Warning (amber-500 — already 7.7:1 on near-black, AAA. No bump needed
     * because yellows are physically easier on dark backgrounds than on light). */
    --interlace-warning: oklch(0.769 0.1647 70.1);
    --interlace-warning-foreground: oklch(0.235 0.0362 290.6);

    /* Info (blue-300 — new semantic. text-info on near-black ≈ 8.7:1 (AAA). */
    --interlace-info: oklch(0.809 0.0956 251.8);
    --interlace-info-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);

    /* Caution (orange-300 — the dark-mode twin of the light orange-900 rung.
     * #fdba74 ≈ 10.9:1 on near-black; against its own `--caution-foreground`
     * (#0a0a0a) the filled chip reads the same 10.9:1, so the pair holds in
     * both directions like every other status token here. */
    --interlace-caution: oklch(0.837 0.1165 66.3);
    --interlace-caution-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);

    /* Highlight (amber-400 — brighter than light mode so the chip still
     * reads as lit on near-black; #0a0a0a on #fbbf24 ≈ 11.9:1, AAA). */
    --interlace-highlight: oklch(0.837 0.1644 84.4);
    --interlace-highlight-foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);

    /* ── Scheme-invariant tokens, restated ──────────────────────────
     * The nine tokens below plus the three radii hold the SAME value in
     * both schemes — a scrim is dark because it sits on a photo, and the
     * cosmic hero paints its own near-black surface in either scheme (see
     * the light block for the full reasoning on each).
     *
     * They are restated here anyway, following the precedent the window
     * controls set below: every theme × scheme block is a COMPLETE
     * override surface. That is what makes `THEME_TOKENS` checkable — a
     * per-scheme block that only carries the tokens which happen to
     * invert gives a forking consumer no way to tell "deliberately the
     * same" apart from "forgotten", and the lock no way to tell either. */
    --interlace-scrim: oklch(0 0 0);
    --interlace-scrim-foreground: oklch(1 0 0);

    --interlace-hero-star: oklch(0.839 0.0877 46.2);   /* brand orange tint — star head */
    --interlace-hero-trail: oklch(0.589 0.13186 159.35);  /* brand green — trail gradient */
    --interlace-hero-meteor: oklch(0.904 0.0515 48.8); /* palest orange — meteor streak */

    --interlace-hero-surface: oklch(0.151 0.0055 67.8);      /* gradient midpoint */
    --interlace-hero-surface-deep: oklch(0 0 0); /* gradient floor */
    --interlace-hero-foreground: oklch(0.947 0.0063 75.4);   /* 16.4:1 on the surface (AAA) */

    /* Radius base — every rounded-* step derives from it (see
     * structure/type.css): sm 8px, md 10px, lg 12px, xl 16px at 0.75rem. */
    --interlace-radius: 0.75rem;

    /* Window controls — macOS ships the same traffic-light hues in dark
     * mode, so these do not invert. Declared here anyway so the dark block
     * is a complete override surface for a forking consumer. */
    --interlace-window-control-close: oklch(0.694 0.1964 26.4);
    --interlace-window-control-minimize: oklch(0.835 0.1612 80.9);
    --interlace-window-control-zoom: oklch(0.728 0.2173 144.7);

    /* Chart palette — lifted lightness so each series stays ≥4.5:1 on
     * `bg-card` (near-black). Same five hues as light, repositioned for
     * dark surfaces. */
    /* Strands — lighter tints of the same pair (chart dark profile) */
    --interlace-strand-a: oklch(0.78 0.14 41);
    --interlace-strand-b: oklch(0.78 0.1 230);

    --interlace-chart-1: oklch(0.78 0.14 41);   /* brand orange */
    --interlace-chart-2: oklch(0.78 0.12 162);  /* brand green */
    --interlace-chart-3: oklch(0.78 0.16 264);  /* blue */
    --interlace-chart-4: oklch(0.78 0.12 90);   /* olive */
    --interlace-chart-5: oklch(0.78 0.11 200);  /* cyan */

    /* Visualisation chrome — dark. Measured against BOTH dark surfaces,
     * because a chart normally renders inside a Card, not on the page:
     *   grid  #2d2823 → 1.36:1 on bg / 1.26:1 on card   DECORATIVE
     *   axis  #746c60 → 3.77:1 on bg / 3.54:1 on card   clears SC 1.4.11 on both
     *   edge  #2d2823 → 1.36:1 on bg / 1.26:1 on card   ambient
     * Perceptual weight matched to light mode (1.39 / 3.64 / 1.39) so a grid
     * does not read as heavier in one theme than the other. */
    --interlace-viz-grid: oklch(0.281 0.0116 67.3);
    --interlace-viz-axis: oklch(0.535 0.0208 78.1);
    --interlace-viz-edge: oklch(0.281 0.0116 67.3);

    /* Brand mark — brighter pair for dark chrome (favicon dark variant). */
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-o: oklch(0.71 0.1634 40.8);
    --interlace-brand-mark-bar-g: oklch(0.589 0.13186 159.35);
  }
}

/*
 * @interlace/ui — STRUCTURE / layout: container widths and the xs rung.
 *
 * Layer 3 of 4 (brand → semantics → structure → page). Spacing is
 * Tailwind's own numeric scale and is not redeclared here.
 *
 * Source: LAYOUT_PHILOSOPHY.md (#2 container widths, #3 spacing) and
 * BREAKPOINT_PHILOSOPHY.md.
 */

@theme {
  /* ── Spacing: Tailwind's numeric scale (p-4, gap-6), which already
     follows the `--spacing` variable. Interlace 2.0 dropped the named
     --spacing-xs…2xl keys: they shadowed max-w-sm/md/lg in every consumer
     app. LAYOUT #3's six steps are 2 / 4 / 6 / 10 / 16 / 24. */

  /* ── Container widths (LAYOUT #2 — four sizes only) ─────────────────
     Generates max-w-prose / max-w-content / max-w-wide. `full` = no max-width
     (omit the utility). ad-hoc max-w-3xl/4xl/5xl/6xl are forbidden by R21. */
  --container-prose: 65ch; /* long-form text */
  --container-content: 64rem; /* 1024px — default landing section */
  --container-wide: 80rem; /* 1280px — card-grid-heavy section */

  /* Floating-surface width. NOT a `Container size` — these three above are
     the page-layout ladder. This one sizes detached chrome (toast stack,
     side-anchored panels) that must stay narrower than any section. Lives
     here rather than as `max-w-[420px]` at the call site so the toast
     stack and anything else that docks to a viewport edge agree on one
     number (R19/R21). */
  --container-float: 26.25rem; /* 420px — edge-docked toast / panel stack */

  /* ── Breakpoints (BREAKPOINT_PHILOSOPHY) ─────────────────────────────
     Tailwind's own ladder (sm 640 / md 768 / lg 1024 / xl 1280 / 2xl 1536)
     is left untouched. Interlace ADDS one tier below it:

       xs = 30rem = 480 CSS px → handheld floor (MIN_VIEWPORT=480)

     `rem`-based so user zoom and browser font-size scaling move it too. */
  --breakpoint-xs: 30rem;
}

## @interlace/interlace-base

9 stylesheets landed in `styles/interlace/`: the `base.css` barrel plus 8 leaves.

Add ONE line to your global stylesheet, after Tailwind:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "./styles/interlace/base.css";
```

This adds tokens and never replaces your own: your `font-sans`, `rounded-*`, breakpoints, spacing and `:root` colours compile exactly as before. Components use your shadcn colours until you add `@interlace/theme`.

The barrel declares the cascade layers and imports the leaves in the one order that works (brand/interlace.css → brand/harbor.css → semantics.css → structure/type.css → structure/layout.css → structure/radius.css → structure/motion.css → structure/scheme.css). Importing the leaves yourself means reproducing that order exactly.

### Token namespace — read this before you theme

This baseline claims **58 `--color-*` keys** plus **47 more** across the `animate`, `breakpoint`, `container`, `ease`, `font`, `leading`, `radius`, `text`, `tracking` namespaces. Tailwind v4 `@theme` keys are global: wherever your app claims the same key, exactly one registration wins — silently, with no diagnostic.

- `--color-accent` — you probably expect the brand highlight colour; you get shadcn’s hover/selected SURFACE — #fef4ed light, #3d1a08 dark. 8:1 lighter than the brand orange beside it. Brand-coloured elements turn near-white. Fails at paint time; no build, type or lint error. Override `--accent (semantics layer) or --interlace-accent (brand layer)`.
- `--color-secondary` — you probably expect a second brand colour; you get a light grey surface — #f5f3f0 light. Secondary buttons and badges lose their colour entirely. Override `--secondary or --interlace-secondary`.
- `--color-muted` — you probably expect de-emphasised TEXT; you get a background tint — #faf7f4 light. Near-white text on white. `--color-muted-foreground` is the text colour. Override `--muted / --muted-foreground`.
- `--color-border` — you probably expect a visible divider; you get #eae7e2 — a deliberate 1.23:1 hairline. It is an intentional AA exemption here, so no contrast gate will flag it. Dividers and card outlines effectively disappear. Override `--border or --interlace-border`.
- `--radius-sm … --radius-xl` — you probably expect Tailwind’s fixed defaults (4/6/8/12px); you get shadcn’s derivation from `--radius` (radius − 4px / − 2px / radius / + 4px), with `--radius` at 0.75rem — 8/10/12/16px. In a shadcn app this is the same derivation the app already has. In a plain Tailwind app, every `rounded-sm…xl` follows `--radius` instead of a fixed value. Override `set --radius (one variable moves every step)`.
- `--font-sans` — you probably expect to be additive; you get a full replacement of Tailwind’s default sans stack. App-wide font change. Override `redeclare --font-sans after the import`.

The colour block is `@theme inline`, so Tailwind substitutes the value into the utility and never emits `--color-*` at runtime. `bg-accent` compiles to `var(--accent)`. Overriding `--color-accent` in your own `:root` therefore has NO effect — override `--accent` (semantics) or `--interlace-accent` (brand) instead.

Full list, per-token values and the migration checklist: https://ds.interlace.tools/theme-authoring#token-namespace

Full contract: https://ds.interlace.tools/css-contract
